text:
Maria: Quick Q — designing KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC). Need recommended pattern for rotating CMKs and rewrapping DEKs for control plane and data-plane w/ zero downtime. Also RBAC + audit logging requirements. Anyone worked through this end-to-end? :eyes:

Ajay: We've done something similar at a previous company. High-level pattern that worked: staged dual-key rollout + metadata-based DEK versioning. Keep it incremental, avoid single-step rewraps on hot tables.

Lisa: can you sketch the sequence? esp. for services that cache DEKs in memory.

Ajay: Sequence (short):
1) Provision new CMK (keyB). Enable key policy/grants for service principals.
2) Update readers/writers to accept a key identifier in object metadata (keyId or dekVersion). Writers start using keyB for new DEKs.
3) Readers first try decrypt with keyB, fallback to keyA if decrypt fails.
4) Start background rewrap workers that ReEncrypt (KMS) DEKs from keyA -> keyB. Mark progress in DB and do in small batches.
5) After all data rewrapped and caches evicted, revoke old grants and deprecate keyA.

Ajay: Important runtime details: cache entries MUST include the dekVersion/key-id so when a rewrap happens the service can evict or try the right key. Avoid long-lived in-memory caches without version metadata.

Ajay: Example grant CLI (use constraints):
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/KeyA\
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-private-data-plane\
  --operations Encrypt Decrypt ReEncryptFrom ReEncryptTo\
  --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"service":"redwood","env":"prod"}\
  --name "redwood-data-plane-grant"
```

Lisa: Audit logging notes: enable CloudTrail for KMS key usage, forward to central SIEM, and tie events to request/trace ids so you can associate a decrypt/encrypt with a specific customer request. Log both control-plane and data-plane events separately.

Lisa: Also, validate encryption context on decrypts. Add enforcement on service side so a decrypt without expected context is rejected (defense-in-depth).

Sam: BYOK / HSM callouts: if a customer imports key material or you're using an HSM-backed CMK, you can't rely on automatic rotation. Instead, create a new CMK and rewrap as above. Document the operations and permissions required for BYOK.

Irene: Re-encryption job considerations: KMS has rate limits and costs. Use an SQS-based worker queue, track item state in DB, idempotent rewraps, exponential backoff for throttles. Do a pilot on cold data first.

Irene: Also build a quick health endpoint for the rewrap job that reports progress (items processed, errors, remaining). Useful for runbooks.

security-bot: Reminder: use grant constraints (EncryptionContextSubset) and permission scoping rather than broad IAM policies where possible. Grants can be time-limited and easier to rotate than long-lived IAM roles. :lock:

deploy-bot: Canary plan suggestion — simulate rotation in staging and then a phasing in prod:
- Phase 0: create keyB and grants, enable readers to accept both keys (feature flag off for writers)
- Phase 1: enable writers in canary cluster (5% traffic) -> monitor errors & latency for 24h
- Phase 2: start rewrap worker on canary dataset and validate reads
- Phase 3: ramp writers to 50% then 100% while rewrap runs in background
- Fallback: re-enable keyA acceptance (already implemented) and reapply grants if needed

deploy-bot: Also prepare a fast rollback: re-add grants for keyA, flip feature flag to force writers to use keyA, and stop the rewrap workers. Test rollback in staging ahead of time.

Maria: These are great. Couple quick RBAC specifics I'm thinking: control plane should have a separate, minimal role that can only Decrypt for token ops and ReEncrypt for scheduled migrations. Data-plane (inference host) should get Decrypt/Encrypt for runtime ops but no IAM to rewrap at scale. Thoughts?

Ajay: 👍 agreed. Principle of least privilege: split roles by function and give the rewrap job a scoped role with re-encrypt permissions and S3/DB access it needs. Control plane gets only what it needs for key management APIs (create, list grants, etc.).

Lisa: Also add CloudTrail Insights on KMS keys for anomaly detection and connect KMS events to your existing incident response runbooks. Tag events with correlation IDs in your logs.

Irene: One more: consider a "dual-dek" period where objects carry both dek ciphertexts (old/new) for extremely hot objects. That reduces latency spikes during rewrap but increases storage. Use for small high-traffic sets only.

Maria: Thanks all — I'll draft a runbook with the phased plan + sample CLI snippets and a simulated rotation checklist. Anyone want to pair on the staging test next Tues? :+1:
